title: Anticoagulant Safety: Bleeding Risk and Monitoring
subject: Prescription Pearls
preview: Anticoagulants reduce thrombosis risk but carry bleeding risk; indication, renal function, interactions and procedure plans matter.
quickRevision: Anticoagulants reduce thrombosis risk but carry bleeding risk; indication, renal function, interactions and procedure plans matter.
Check concomitant antiplatelets, NSAIDs and bleeding history, and document the plan for missed doses or procedures.
Bleeding management depends on severity, timing of the last dose and anticoagulant-specific reversal availability.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Anticoagulants reduce thrombosis risk but carry bleeding risk; indication, renal function, interactions and procedure plans matter.
Warfarin is monitored with INR; direct oral anticoagulants generally do not use INR as routine therapeutic monitoring.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Check concomitant antiplatelets, NSAIDs and bleeding history, and document the plan for missed doses or procedures.
Bleeding management depends on severity, timing of the last dose and anticoagulant-specific reversal availability.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A normal INR does not prove that a direct oral anticoagulant has no effect.

quiz.question: Which test is routinely used to monitor warfarin?
quiz.explanation: Warfarin is monitored with INR; direct oral anticoagulants generally do not use INR as routine therapeutic monitoring.
